}\n490\t\n491\t    /// Single supervisor tick: poll queue and spawn workers if needed.\n492\t    ///\n493\t    /// Returns true if a worker was spawned, false otherwise.\n494\t    async fn tick(&mut Spawn a new worker process.\n565\t    async fn spawn_worker(&self, ready_count: usize) -> Result<()> {\n566\t        // Phase 1: resource check before worker spawn.\n567\t        // Check system resources (CPU and memory) before spawning a worker.\n568\t        // If saturated, retry with bounded backoff rather than proceeding into\n569\t        // a launch that may be killed by the OS due to resource pressure.\n570\t        const MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS: u64 = 120; // Maximum total wait time\n571\t        const RESOURCE_RETRY_DELAY_SECS: u64 = 5; // Initial retry delay\n572\t        let accumulate as `<defunct>`\n743\t/// zombies for the lifetime of the supervisor daemon.\n744\t///\n745\t/// Safe to call unconditionally every tick: `needle supervise` only ever\n746\t/// directly spawns worker processes — gate commands and dispatch\n747\t/// subprocesses are spawned by the *worker* process, a separate PID tree —\n748\t/// so a blind `waitpid(-1, ...)` here cannot race with `.wait()` calls\n749\t/// elsewhere in the codebase (`dispatch`/`telemetry`/`canary`), which all\n750\t/// run in different processes. See ADR-010 / GH #12.\n751\t#[cfg(unix)]\n752\tfn reap_zombie_children() {\n753\t    reap_children_matching(-1);\n754\t}\n755\t\n756\t#[cfg(not(unix))]\n757\tfn reap_zombie_children() {}\n758\t\n759\t/// Shared implementation of the `WNOHANG` reap loop, parameterized by which\n760\t/// PID to wait on (`-1` in production, meaning \"any direct child\" — see\n761\t/// `reap_zombie_children`). Split out so tests can exercise the exact same\n762\t/// loop scoped to a single PID they spawned themselves, instead of calling\n763\t/// the crate-wide `-1` sweep from inside the shared `cargo test --lib`\n764\t/// process, where it could reap an unrelated concurrently-running test's own\n765\t/// child (unit tests across the whole crate share one process/many threads,\n766\t/// unlike separate integration-test binaries).\n767\t#[cfg(unix)]\n768\tfn reap_children_matching(target_pid: libc::pid_t) {\n769\t    loop {\n770\t        let mut status: libc::c_int = 0;\n771\t        // SAFETY: waitpid(target_pid, &mut status, WNOHANG) reaps an\n772\t        // already-exited child (any direct child, if target_pid == -1)\n773\t        // without blocking; `status` is a valid stack-local out parameter\n774\t        // for the duration of the call.\n775\t        let pid = unsafe { libc::waitpid(target_pid, &mut status, libc::WNOHANG) };\n776\t        match pid {\n777\t            0 => break,          // No exited children ready to reap right now.\n778\t            n if n < 0 => break, // ECHILD (no children) or another errno; stop for this tick.\n779\t            n => tracing::debug!(reaped_pid = n, \"reaped exited worker child\"),\n780\t        }\n781\t    }\n782\t}\n783\t\n784\t/// Run the supervisor from the CLI.\n785\t///\n786\t/// This is the entry point for ──\n1141\t\n1142\t    #[cfg(unix)]\n1143\t    #[test]\n1144\t    fn reap_zombie_children_reaps_an_exited_child() {\n1145\t        // Exercises reap_children_matching (the exact loop reap_zombie_children\n1146\t        // wraps) scoped to a PID we spawned ourselves — NOT the real\n1147\t        // reap_zombie_children()'s `-1` (any child) target. Unit tests across\n1148\t        // the whole crate share one process/many threads under `cargo test\n1149\t        // --lib`; calling the `-1` sweep here could reap an unrelated,\n1150\t        // concurrently-running test's own child out from under it. Scoping to\n1151\t        // our own PID exercises the identical waitpid/WNOHANG logic with none\n1152\t        // of that collision risk.\n1153\t        //\n1154\t        // Spawn a real short-lived child directly (no setsid/detach — this\n1155\t        // test process is its real parent).\n1156\t        let child = std::process::Command::new(\"true\")\n1157\t            .spawn()\n1158\t            .expect(\"failed to spawn `true`\");\n1159\t        let pid = child.id();\n1160\t\n1161\t        // Wait for it to actually exit (without reaping it — do not call\n1162\t        // child.wait() here, that would reap it ourselves and defeat the test).\n1163\t        let stat_path = format!(\"/proc/{pid}/stat\");\n1164\t        let mut became_zombie = false;\n1165\t        for _ in 0..200 {\n1166\t            if let Ok(stat) = std::fs::read_to_string(&stat_path) {\n1167\t                if let Some(after_comm) = stat.rfind(')') {\n1168\t                    if stat[after_comm + 1..].trim_start().starts_with('Z') {\n1169\t                        became_zombie = true;\n1170\t                        break;\n1171\t                    }\n1172\t                }\n1173\t            } else {\n1174\t                // Already reaped by something else, or /proc entry gone —\n1175\t                // can't validate the pre-condition; skip rather than false-fail.\n1176\t                break;\n1177\t            }\n1178\t            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(10));\n1179\t        }\n1180\t        assert!(\n1181\t            became_zombie,\n1182\t            \"child did not reach zombie state before timeout — test precondition not met\"\n1183\t        );\n1184\t\n1185\t        reap_children_matching(pid as libc::pid_t);\n1186\t\n1187\t        // After reaping, /proc/<pid> should no longer exist.\n1188\t        assert!(\n1189\t            !std::path::Path::new(&stat_path).exists(),\n1190\t            \"child was not reaped: {stat_path} still exists\"\n1191\t        );\n1192\t\n1193\t        // Prevent a double-wait/drop warning: the child is already reaped by\n1194\t        // our sweep, so explicitly forget rather than calling child.wait().\n1195\t        std::mem::forget(child);\n1196\t    }\n1197\t\n1198\t    // ── Supervisor startup resolved path logging test (bf-5hnpy) ──\n1199\t\n1200\t    #[tokio::test]\n1201\t            telemetry,\n            shutdown: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Run the supervisor loop until shutdown is signaled.\n    pub async fn run(mut self) -> Result<()> {\n        // Install signal handlers for graceful shutdown\n        let shutdown = self.shutdown.clone();\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        {\n            // Handle SIGINT and SIGTERM\n            std::mem::drop(tokio::spawn(async move {\n                use tokio::signal::unix::{signal, SignalKind};\n                let mut sigint =\n                    signal(SignalKind::interrupt()).expect(\"failed to setup SIGINT handler\");\n                let mut sigterm =\n                    signal(SignalKind::terminate()).expect(\"failed to setup SIGTERM handler\");\n\n                tokio::select! {\n                    _ = sigint.recv() => {\n                        tracing::info!(\"received SIGINT, shutting down supervisor\");\n                        shutdown.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);\n                    }\n                    _ = sigterm.recv() => {\n                        tracing::info!(\"received SIGTERM, shutting down supervisor\");\n                        shutdown.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);\n                    }\n                }\n            }));\n        }\n\n        #[cfg(not(unix))]\n        {\n            // Handle Ctrl+C on non-Unix platforms\n            let _ = tokio::spawn(async move {\n                if tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await.is_ok() {\n                    tracing::info!(\"received Ctrl+C, shutting down supervisor\");\n                    shutdown.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);\n                }\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Start telemetry\n        self.telemetry.start();\n\n        // Emit worker binary resolved event (fixes GitHub issue jedarden/NEEDLE#11)\n        let worker_binary = resolve_worker_binary(self.config.worker_binary_path.clone())\n            .context(\"failed to resolve worker binary path for supervisor\")?;\n        let binary_source = if self.config.worker_binary_path.is_some() {\n            \"config override (worker.worker_binary_path)\"\n        } else {\n            \"current_exe()\"\n        };\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorBinaryResolved {\n            worker_binary: worker_binary.display().to_string(),\n            source: binary_source.to_string(),\n        })?;\n\n        // Emit supervisor started event\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorStarted {\n            workspace: self.config.workspace.display().to_string(),\n            max_workers: self.config.max_workers,\n        })?;\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            workspace = %self.config.workspace.display(),\n            max_workers = self.config.max_workers,\n            poll_interval_secs = self.config.poll_interval_secs,\n            \"supervisor started\"\n        );\n\n        let mut consecutive_errors = 0u32;\n        let mut last_spawn_time = Instant::now();\n        let mut total_spawned = 0u64;\n        let mut total_polls = 0u64;\n\n        // Main supervisor loop\n        loop {\n            // Check for shutdown signal\n            if self.shutdown.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {\n                tracing::info!(\"shutdown signal received, stopping supervisor\");\n                break;\n            }\n\n            // Enforce spawn backoff\n            let backoff_remaining = last_spawn_time.elapsed().as_secs();\n            if backoff_remaining < SPAWN_BACKOFF_SECS {\n                let wait_secs = SPAWN_BACKOFF_SECS - backoff_remaining;\n                tracing::debug!(wait_secs, \"in spawn backoff, waiting before next poll\");\n                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(wait_secs)).await;\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Poll the ready queue and check fleet state\n            total_polls += 1;\n\n            // Emit summary every 60 ticks (approximately 10 minutes at default interval)\n            if total_polls % 60 == 0 {\n                let active_workers = self.registry.list().unwrap_or_default();\n                let ready_beads = self\n                    .store\n                    .ready(&Filters::default())\n                    .await\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorSummary {\n                    polls: total_polls,\n                    spawned: total_spawned,\n                    total_workers: active_workers.len() as u32,\n                    ready_beads: ready_beads.len() as u32,\n                });\n            }\n\n            match self.tick().await {\n                Ok(spawned) => {\n                    consecutive_errors = 0;\n                    if spawned {\n                        total_spawned += 1;\n                        last_spawn_time = Instant::now();\n                    }\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    consecutive_errors += 1;\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        error = %e,\n                        consecutive_errors = consecutive_errors,\n                        \"supervisor tick failed\"\n                    );\n\n                    // Emit spawn failed event\n                    let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorSpawnFailed {\n                        error: e.to_string(),\n                    });\n\n                    // Enter long backoff if error threshold exceeded\n                    if consecutive_errors >= MAX_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            consecutive_errors,\n                            backoff_secs = ERROR_BACKOFF_SECS,\n                            \"error threshold exceeded, entering long backoff\"\n                        );\n\n                        // Emit backoff event\n                        let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorBackoff {\n                            backoff_secs: ERROR_BACKOFF_SECS,\n                            consecutive_failures: consecutive_errors,\n                        });\n\n                        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(ERROR_BACKOFF_SECS)).await;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Wait before next poll\n            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(self.config.poll_interval_secs)).await;\n        }\n\n        // Emit supervisor stopped event\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorStopped {\n            reason: \"shutdown_requested\".to_string(),\n        })?;\n\n        // Shutdown telemetry\n        self.telemetry.shutdown().await;\n\n        tracing::info!(\"supervisor stopped\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Single supervisor tick: poll queue and spawn workers if needed.\n    ///\n    /// Returns true if a worker was spawned, false otherwise.\n    async fn tick(&mut self) -> Result<bool> {\n        reap_zombie_children();\n\n        // Get active workers\n        let active_workers = self.registry.list().unwrap_or_default();\n        let active_count = active_workers.len() as u32;\n\n        // Filter out dead workers (PID no longer alive)\n        let alive_workers: Vec<_> = active_workers\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|w| is_pid_alive(w.pid))\n            .collect();\n\n        // Update registry to remove dead workers\n        if alive_workers.len() < active_workers.len() {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                removed = active_count - alive_workers.len() as u32,\n                \"cleaning up dead workers from registry\"\n            );\n            for worker in &active_workers {\n                if !is_pid_alive(worker.pid) {\n                    let _ = self.registry.deregister(&worker.id);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let alive_count = alive_workers.len() as u32;\n\n        // Check if we're at capacity\n        if alive_count >= self.config.max_workers {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                alive_count,\n                max_workers = self.config.max_workers,\n                \"fleet at capacity, no spawning needed\"\n            );\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n\n        // Poll the ready queue\n        let filters = Filters::default();\n        let ready_beads = self.store.ready(&filters).await?;\n\n        // If queue is empty, no need to spawn\n        if ready_beads.is_empty() {\n            tracing::debug!(\"ready queue empty, no spawning needed\");\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n\n        // We have ready beads and capacity: spawn a worker\n        let ready_count = ready_beads.len();\n        tracing::info!(\n            ready_beads = ready_count,\n            active_workers = alive_count,\n            max_workers = self.config.max_workers,\n            \"ready beads detected with capacity, spawning worker\"\n        );\n\n        // Emit spawn decision event\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorSpawnDecision {\n            to_spawn: 1,\n            ready_beads: ready_count as u32,\n            max_workers: self.config.max_workers,\n        })?;\n\n        // Spawn the worker\n        self.spawn_worker(ready_count).await?;\n\n        Ok(true)\n    }\n\n    /// Spawn a new worker process.\n    async fn spawn_worker(&self, ready_count: usize) -> Result<()> {\n        // Phase 1: resource check before worker spawn.\n        // Check system resources (CPU and memory) before spawning a worker.\n        // If saturated, retry with bounded backoff rather than proceeding into\n        // a launch that may be killed by the OS due to resource pressure.\n        const MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS: u64 = 120; // Maximum total wait time\n        const RESOURCE_RETRY_DELAY_SECS: u64 = 5; // Initial retry delay\n        let mut resource_wait_total = 0u64;\n        let mut resource_retry_delay = RESOURCE_RETRY_DELAY_SECS;\n\n        loop {\n            match crate::rate_limit::RateLimiter::check_system_resources_for_launch(\n                self.needle_config.worker.cpu_load_warn,\n                self.needle_config.worker.memory_free_warn_mb,\n                &self.telemetry,\n            ) {\n                Ok(()) => {\n                    // Resources are acceptable, proceed to spawn\n                    break;\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    if resource_wait_total >= MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS {\n                        // Still saturated after max wait, fail the spawn explicitly\n                        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorSpawnFailed {\n                            error: format!(\n                                \"system still saturated after {}s wait: {}\",\n                                MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS, e\n                            ),\n                        })?;\n                        bail!(\n                            \"worker spawn deferred {} times ({}s total wait), system still saturated: {}. Spawn aborted — retry when load drops\",\n                            resource_wait_total / resource_retry_delay,\n                            resource_wait_total,\n                            e\n                        );\n                    }\n\n                    // Resources are saturated, wait and retry\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        error = %e,\n                        wait_secs = resource_retry_delay,\n                        total_waited_secs = resource_wait_total,\n                        \"system resources saturated, deferring worker spawn\"\n                    );\n\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorSpawnFailed {\n                        error: format!(\"system saturated: {}\", e),\n                    })?;\n\n                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(resource_retry_delay)).await;\n                    resource_wait_total += resource_retry_delay;\n\n                    // Exponential backoff with cap at 30 seconds\n                    resource_retry_delay = std::cmp::min(resource_retry_delay * 2, 30);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let worker_id = self.generate_worker_id()?;\n        let agent_name = self\n            .config\n            .agent\n            .as_ref()\n            .unwrap_or(&self.needle_config.agent.default)\n            .clone();\n\n        // Resolve the worker binary path. Call resolve_worker_binary() instead\n        // of hardcoding 'needle' to ensure the correct binary is spawned.\n        // Handle resolution errors gracefully by logging and returning an error.\n        let worker_binary = resolve_worker_binary(self.config.worker_binary_path.clone())\n            .with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"failed to resolve worker binary path for worker {}\",\n                    worker_id\n                )\n            })?;\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            worker_id = %worker_id,\n            agent = %agent_name,\n            worker_binary = %worker_binary.display(),\n            \"spawning worker\"\n        );\n\n        // Spawn the worker process (platform-agnostic) with retry wrapper to\n        // handle ETXTBSY (errno 26) which can occur when spawning a worker binary\n        // that was written to disk immediately before execution (race condition\n        // between write close and kernel page cache sync). This is especially\n        // common after hot-reload or upgrade.\n        //\n        // Uses the resolved worker binary path (current_exe() by default) rather\n        // than a bare PATH lookup of \"needle\" — see GitHub issue jedarden/NEEDLE#11.\n        let _child = crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential_child(\n            || {\n                let mut cmd = std::process::Command::new(&worker_binary);\n                cmd.arg(\"run\")\n                    .arg(\"--workspace\")\n                    .arg(&self.config.workspace)\n                    .arg(\"--agent\")\n                    .arg(&agent_name)\n                    .arg(\"--identifier\")\n                    .arg(&worker_id)\n                    .arg(\"--count\")\n                    .arg(\"1\");\n\n                if let Some(timeout) = self.config.agent_timeout {\n                    cmd.arg(\"--timeout\").arg(timeout.to_string());\n                }\n\n                // Spawn in background (detached process)\n                cmd.stdin(std::process::Stdio::null())\n                    .stdout(std::process::Stdio::null())\n                    .stderr(std::process::Stdio::null());\n\n                #[cfg(unix)]\n                {\n                    use std::os::unix::process::CommandExt;\n                    cmd.process_group(0);\n\n                    // On Unix, use setsid to create a new session\n                    unsafe {\n                        cmd.pre_exec(|| {\n                            libc::setsid();\n                            Ok(())\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n\n                cmd.spawn()\n            },\n            10,\n            20,\n        )?;\n\n        // Emit worker spawned event\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorWorkerSpawned {\n            ready_count,\n            total_spawned: 1,\n        })?;\n\n        tracing::info!(worker_id = %worker_id, \"worker spawned successfully\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Generate a unique worker identifier not currently in use.\n    fn generate_worker_id(&self) -> Result<String> {\n        const NATO_ALPHABET: &[&str] = &[\n            \"alpha\", \"bravo\", \"charlie\", \"delta\", \"echo\", \"foxtrot\", \"golf\", \"hotel\", \"india\",\n            \"juliet\", \"kilo\", \"lima\", \"mike\", \"november\", \"oscar\", \"papa\", \"quebec\", \"romeo\",\n            \"sierra\", \"tango\", \"uniform\", \"victor\", \"whiskey\", \"xray\", \"yankee\", \"zulu\",\n        ];\n\n        let active = self.registry.list().unwrap_or_default();\n        let occupied: std::collections::HashSet<String> = active\n            .iter()\n            .map(|w| w.id.split('-').next_back().unwrap_or(&w.id).to_string())\n            .collect();\n\n        for name in NATO_ALPHABET {\n            if !occupied.contains(*name) {\n                return Ok(name.to_string());\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Fallback: use a numbered suffix\n        for i in 1..=100 {\n            let name = format!(\"worker{}\", i);\n            if !occupied.contains(&name) {\n                return Ok(name);\n            }\n        }\n\n        anyhow::bail!(\"unable to generate unique worker identifier\")\n    }\n}\n\n/// Reap any exited direct children of this process (workers spawned by\n/// `Supervisor::spawn_worker`) so they don't accumulate as `<defunct>`\n/// zombies for the lifetime of the supervisor daemon.\n///\n/// Safe to call unconditionally every tick: `needle supervise` only ever\n/// directly spawns worker processes — gate commands and dispatch\n/// subprocesses are spawned by the *worker* process, a separate PID tree —\n/// so a blind `waitpid(-1, ...)` here cannot race with `.wait()` calls\n/// elsewhere in the codebase (`dispatch`/`telemetry`/`canary`), which all\n/// run in different processes. See ADR-010 / GH #12.\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn reap_zombie_children() {\n    reap_children_matching(-1);\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(unix))]\nfn reap_zombie_children() {}\n\n/// Shared implementation of the `WNOHANG` reap loop, parameterized by which\n/// PID to wait on (`-1` in production, meaning \"any direct child\" — see\n/// `reap_zombie_children`). Split out so tests can exercise the exact same\n/// loop scoped to a single PID they spawned themselves, instead of calling\n/// the crate-wide `-1` sweep from inside the shared `cargo test --lib`\n/// process, where it could reap an unrelated concurrently-running test's own\n/// child (unit tests across the whole crate share one process/many threads,\n/// unlike separate integration-test binaries).\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn reap_children_matching(target_pid: libc::pid_t) {\n    loop {\n        let mut status: libc::c_int = 0;\n        // SAFETY: waitpid(target_pid, &mut status, WNOHANG) reaps an\n        // already-exited child (any direct child, if target_pid == -1)\n        // without blocking; `status` is a valid stack-local out parameter\n        // for the duration of the call.\n        let pid = unsafe { libc::waitpid(target_pid, &mut status, libc::WNOHANG) };\n        match pid {\n            0 => break,          // No exited children ready to reap right now.\n            n if n < 0 => break, // ECHILD (no children) or another errno; stop for this tick.\n            n => tracing::debug!(reaped_pid = n, \"reaped exited worker child\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Run the supervisor from the CLI.\n///\n/// This is the entry point for `needle supervise`.\npub async fn run_supervisor(workspace_opt: Option<PathBuf>) -> Result<()> {\n    // Determine workspace\n    let workspace_root = if let Some(ws) = workspace_opt {\n        ws.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| ws.clone())\n    } else {\n        let global = ConfigLoader::load_global()?;\n        global.workspace.default.clone()\n    };\n\n    // Load full config\n    let cli_overrides = CliOverrides {\n        workspace: Some(workspace_root.clone()),\n        ..Default::default()\n    };\n    let (config, _) = ConfigLoader::load_resolved(&workspace_root, cli_overrides)?;\n\n    // Build supervisor config\n    let supervisor_config = SupervisorConfig {\n        workspace: workspace_root.clone(),\n        max_workers: config.worker.max_workers,\n        poll_interval_secs: DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_SECS,\n        agent: Some(config.agent.default.clone()),\n        agent_timeout: Some(config.agent.timeout),\n        worker_binary_path: config.worker.worker_binary_path.clone(),\n    };\n\n    // Create and run supervisor\n    let supervisor = Supervisor::new(supervisor_config, config)?;\n    supervisor.run().await\n}\n\n// ─── Tests issue jedarden/NEEDLE#12) ──\n\n    #[cfg(unix)]\n    #[test]\n    fn reap_zombie_children_reaps_an_exited_child() {\n        // Exercises reap_children_matching (the exact loop reap_zombie_children\n        // wraps) scoped to a PID we spawned ourselves — NOT the real\n        // reap_zombie_children()'s `-1` (any child) target. Unit tests across\n        // the whole crate share one process/many threads under `cargo test\n        // --lib`; calling the `-1` sweep here could reap an unrelated,\n        // concurrently-running test's own child out from under it. Scoping to\n        // our own PID exercises the identical waitpid/WNOHANG logic with none\n        // of that collision risk.\n        //\n        // Spawn a real short-lived child directly (no setsid/detach — this\n        // test process is its real parent).\n        let child = std::process::Command::new(\"true\")\n            .spawn()\n            .expect(\"failed to spawn `true`\");\n        let pid = child.id();\n\n        // Wait for it to actually exit (without reaping it — do not call\n        // child.wait() here, that would reap it ourselves and defeat the test).\n        let stat_path = format!(\"/proc/{pid}/stat\");\n        let mut became_zombie = false;\n        for _ in 0..200 {\n            if let Ok(stat) = std::fs::read_to_string(&stat_path) {\n                if let Some(after_comm) = stat.rfind(')') {\n                    if stat[after_comm + 1..].trim_start().starts_with('Z') {\n                        became_zombie = true;\n                        break;\n                    }\n                }\n            } else {\n                // Already reaped by something else, or /proc entry gone —\n                // can't validate the pre-condition; skip rather than false-fail.\n                break;\n            }\n            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(10));\n        }\n        assert!(\n            became_zombie,\n            \"child did not reach zombie state before timeout — test precondition not met\"\n        );\n\n        reap_children_matching(pid as libc::pid_t);\n\n        // After reaping, /proc/<pid> should no longer exist.\n        assert!(\n            !std::path::Path::new(&stat_path).exists(),\n            \"child was not reaped: {stat_path} still exists\"\n        );\n\n        // Prevent a double-wait/drop warning: the child is already reaped by\n        // our sweep, so explicitly forget rather than calling child.wait().\n        std::mem::forget(child);\n    }\n\n    // ── Supervisor Writes heartbeat at each interval.\n1188\t///\n1189\t/// Circuit breaker: after `max_consecutive_failures` consecutive write failures\n1190\t/// the loop sets the shutdown flag and exits so the worker terminates instead of\n1191\t/// spinning indefinitely.\n1192\t///\n1193\t/// Backoff: each consecutive failure doubles the inter-attempt sleep, capped at\n1194\t/// [`MAX_HEARTBEAT_BACKOFF`].\n1195\t///\n1196\t/// Uses an interruptible sleep pattern to respond quickly to shutdown signals.\n1197\t#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\n1198\tfn emitter_loop(\n1199\t    shared_state: Arc<Mutex<SharedHeartbeatState>>,\n1200\t    shutdown: Arc<AtomicBool>,\n1201\t    heartbeat_dir: PathBuf,\n1202\t    worker_id: String,\n1203\t    qualified_id: String,\n1204\t    workspace: PathBuf,\n1205\t    started_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n1206\t    interval: Duration,\n1207\t    max_consecutive_failures: u32,\n1208\t) {\n1209\t    // Ensure the heartbeat directory exists before entering the write loop so\n1210\t    // that workers self-recover if ~/.needle/state/heartbeats/ is deleted.\n1211\t    if let Err(e) = std::fs::create_dir_all(&heartbeat_dir) {\n1212\t        tracing::error!(\n1213\t            error = %e,\n1214\t            dir = %heartbeat_dir.display(),\n1215\t            \"failed to create heartbeat directory\"\n1216\t        );\n1217\t    }\n1218\t\n1219\t    let mut consecutive_failures: u32 = 0;\n1220\t    let mut current_sleep = interval;\n1221\t    let mut elapsed = Duration::ZERO;\n1222\t\n1223\t    loop {\n1224\t        // Interruptible sleep: check shutdown flag every 100ms instead of\n1225\t        // sleeping for the full interval. This ensures the emitter responds\n1226\t        // to shutdown signals quickly, giving the atexit handler a chance to\n1227\t        // emit worker.stopped telemetry even if the process is killed.\n1228\t        while elapsed < current_sleep {\n1229\t            if shutdown.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {\n1230\t                tracing::debug!(worker = %worker_id, \"heartbeat emitter shutting down\");\n1231\t                return;\n1232\t            }\n1233\t            let sleep_dur = std::cmp::min(INTERRUPTIBLE_SLEEP_INTERVAL, current_sleep - elapsed);\n1234\t            std::thread::sleep(sleep_dur);\n1235\t            elapsed += sleep_dur;\n1236\t        }\n1237\t        elapsed = Duration::ZERO;\n1238\t\n1239\t        let (state, current_bead, beads_processed, current_workspace, model) =\n1240\t            match shared_state.lock() {\n1241\t                Ok(guard) => (\n1242\t                    guard.state.clone(),\n1243\t                    guard.current_bead.clone(),\n1244\t                    guard.beads_processed,\n1245\t                    guard.current_workspace.clone(),\n1246\t                    guard.model.clone(),\n1247\t                ),\n1248\t                Err(_) => {\n1249\t                    // Mutex poisoned — the main thread panicked. Exit.\n1250\t                    tracing::error!(\n1251\t                        worker = %worker_id,\n1252\t                        \"shared state mutex poisoned, heartbeat emitter exiting\"\n1253\t                    );\n1254\t                    return;\n1255\t                }\n1256\t            };\n1257\t\n1258\t        // Use the current bead's workspace if set, otherwise fall back to home workspace.\n1259\t        let effective_workspace = current_workspace.unwrap_or_else(|| workspace.clone());\n1260\t\n1261\t        let is_idle = state == WorkerState::Exhausted || current_bead.is_none();\n1262\t        let current_task = current_bead.as_ref().map(|b| b.to_string());\n1263\t\n1264\t        let data = HeartbeatData {\n1265\t            worker_id: worker_id.clone(),\n1266\t            qualified_id: qualified_id.clone(),\n1267\t            pid: std::process::id(),\n1268\t            state,\n1269\t            current_bead,\n1270\t            workspace: effective_workspace,\n1271\t            last_heartbeat: Utc::now(),\n1272\t            started_at,\n1273\t            beads_processed,\n1274\t            session: worker_id.clone(),\n1275\t            is_idle,\n1276\t            current_task,\n1277\t            model,\n1278\t            heartbeat_file: None,\n1279\t        };\n1280\t\n1281\t        let path = heartbeat_dir.join(format!(\"{}.json\", qualified_id));\n1282\t        let tmp_path = path.with_extension(\"json.tmp\");\n1283\t\n1284\t        let write_result: anyhow::Result<()> = (|| {\n1285\t            // Re-assert the heartbeat directory on every attempt, not just once\n1286\t            // before the loop starts. If the directory (or an ancestor) is\n1287\t            // transiently removed or unavailable while the worker is running —\n1288\t            // e.g. an external cleanup process, a race with another tool, or a\n1289\t            // filesystem hiccup under load — the write below would otherwise\n1290\t            // fail with ENOENT on every subsequent attempt until the circuit\n1291\t            // breaker trips, since nothing else recreates it. `create_dir_all`\n1292\t            // is a cheap no-op when the directory already exists, so doing this\n1293\t            // unconditionally lets a default\n1296\t            // backoff schedule, can take 25-30 minutes to trigger).\n1297\t            std::fs::create_dir_all(&heartbeat_dir)?;\n1298\t            let json = })();\n1303\t\n1304\t        match write_result {\n1305\t            Ok(()) => {\n1306\t                consecutive_failures = 0;\n1307\t                current_sleep = interval;\n1308\t            }\n1309\t            Err(e) => {\n1310\t                consecutive_failures += 1;\n1311\t                tracing::error!(\n1312\t                    error = %e,\n1313\t                    worker = %worker_id,\n1314\t                    consecutive_failures,\n1315\t                    max = max_consecutive_failures,\n1316\t                    \"heartbeat write failed\"\n1317\t                );\n1318\t                if consecutive_failures >= max_consecutive_failures {\n1319\t                    tracing::error!(\n1320\t                        worker = %worker_id,\n1321\t                        consecutive_failures,\n1322\t                        \"heartbeat emitter circuit breaker triggered — worker will shut down\"\n1323\t                    );\n1324\t                    // Emit a final heartbeat event before shutting down so the\n1325\t                    // telemetry log shows the circuit breaker was the cause.\n1326\t                    let _ = std::fs::write(\n1327\t                        heartbeat_dir.join(format!(\"{}-circuit-breaker.txt\", qualified_id)),\n1328\t                        format!(\n1329\t                            \"Circuit breaker tripped after {} consecutive heartbeat write failures\\n\\\n1330\t                             Worker: {}\\n\\\n1331\t                             Qualified ID: {}\\n\\\n1332\t                             Last error: {}\\n\\\n1333\t                             Timestamp: {}\",\n1334\t                            consecutive_failures,\n1335\t                            worker_id,\n1336\t active workers in fleet\"\n            );\n            return Ok(true);\n        }\n\n        // Check for recent spawn activity: any worker started within the last 5 minutes\n        // (excluding ourselves, as we just started)\n        let five_minutes_ago = Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::seconds(300);\n        let recent_spawns: Vec<_> = fresh_workers\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|hb| hb.qualified_id != self.qualified_id)\n            .filter(|hb| hb.started_at > five_minutes_ago)\n            .collect();\n\n        if !recent_spawns.is_empty() {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                recent_spawn_count = recent_spawns.len(),\n                \"supervisor detected: recent worker spawn activity\"\n            );\n            return Ok(true);\n        }\n\n        // No supervisor presence detected\n        tracing::debug!(\"no supervisor detected: single worker, no recent spawn activity\");\n        Ok(false)\n    }\n\n    /// Check for a supervisor heartbeat file at the standard location.\n    ///\n    /// This function provides direct supervisor presence detection by checking\n    /// for a supervisor-specific heartbeat file, separate from worker heartbeats.\n    ///\n    /// The supervisor heartbeat file is expected at:\n    /// `<heartbeat_dir>/supervisor-heartbeat.json`\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Ok(true)` if a fresh supervisor heartbeat file exists,\n    /// `Ok(false)` if no supervisor heartbeat is found or it's stale.\n    /// Returns `Err` if the heartbeat directory cannot be read.\n    ///\n    /// A heartbeat is considered fresh if updated within the last 2 minutes.\n    pub fn check_supervisor_heartbeat_file(&self) -> Result<bool> {\n        let supervisor_hb_path = self.heartbeat_dir.join(\"supervisor-heartbeat.json\");\n\n        // Check if supervisor heartbeat file exists\n        if !supervisor_hb_path.exists() {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                path = %supervisor_hb_path.display(),\n                \"supervisor heartbeat file not found\"\n            );\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n\n        // Read and parse the supervisor heartbeat file\n        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&supervisor_hb_path).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to read supervisor heartbeat file: {}\",\n                supervisor_hb_path.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        // Parse as JSON to verify it's valid (we don't need specific fields)\n        let parsed: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&content).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to parse supervisor heartbeat file: {}\",\n                supervisor_hb_path.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        // Check if heartbeat has a timestamp field\n        let last_heartbeat = if let Some(ts) = parsed.get(\"last_heartbeat\").and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n        {\n            DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(ts)\n                .with_context(|| {\n                    format!(\n                        \"invalid timestamp in supervisor heartbeat file: {}\",\n                        supervisor_hb_path.display()\n                    )\n                })?\n                .with_timezone(&Utc)\n        } else {\n            // No timestamp field - assume file exists but is stale/invalid\n            tracing::debug!(\n                path = %supervisor_hb_path.display(),\n                \"supervisor heartbeat file missing timestamp field\"\n            );\n            return Ok(false);\n        };\n\n        // Check if heartbeat is fresh (within 2 minutes)\n        let age = Utc::now()\n            .signed_duration_since(last_heartbeat)\n            .to_std()\n            .unwrap_or(Duration::ZERO);\n        let supervisor_ttl = Duration::from_secs(120); // 2 minutes\n\n        if age <= supervisor_ttl {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                path = %supervisor_hb_path.display(),\n                age_secs = age.as_secs(),\n                \"fresh supervisor heartbeat detected\"\n            );\n            Ok(true)\n        } else {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                path = %supervisor_hb_path.display(),\n                age_secs = age.as_secs(),\n                ttl_secs = supervisor_ttl.as_secs(),\n                \"supervisor heartbeat is stale\"\n            );\n            Ok(false)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Check for a supervisor socket at the standard location.\n    ///\n    /// This function provides direct supervisor presence detection by checking\n    /// for a Unix domain socket that the supervisor may be listening on.\n    ///\n    /// The socket is expected at: `/tmp/needle-supervisor.sock` or a path\n    /// specified in the `NEEDLE_SUPERVISOR_SOCKET` environment variable.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Ok(true)` if a socket exists at the expected location,\n    /// `Ok(false)` if no socket is found.\n    /// Returns `Err` if socket path cannot be accessed.\n    pub fn check_supervisor_socket() -> Result<bool> {\n        let socket_path = std::env::var(\"NEEDLE_SUPERVISOR_SOCKET\")\n            .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"/tmp/needle-supervisor.sock\".to_string());\n\n        let path = PathBuf::from(&socket_path);\n\n        // Check if socket exists and is a socket file\n        match std::fs::metadata(&path) {\n            Ok(metadata) => {\n                #[cfg(unix)]\n                {\n                    use std::os::unix::fs::FileTypeExt;\n                    let file_type = metadata.file_type();\n                    if file_type.is_socket() {\n                        tracing::debug!(\n                            path = %path.display(),\n                            \"supervisor socket detected\"\n                        );\n                        return Ok(true);\n                    }\n                }\n\n                #[cfg(not(unix))]\n                {\n                    // On non-Unix platforms, just check if the file/path exists\n                    if path.exists() {\n                        tracing::debug!(\n                            path = %path.display(),\n                            \"supervisor socket path exists (non-Unix)\"\n                        );\n                        return Ok(true);\n                    }\n                }\n\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    path = %path.display(),\n                    \"path exists but is not a socket\"\n                );\n                Ok(false)\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    path = %path.display(),\n                    \"supervisor socket not found\"\n                );\n                Ok(false)\n            }\n            Err(e) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n                \"failed to access supervisor socket {}: {}\",\n                path.display(),\n                e\n            )),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Detect supervisor presence using direct checks.\n    ///\n    /// This function combines direct supervisor detection methods:\n    /// 1. Checks for a supervisor heartbeat file\n    /// 2. Checks for a supervisor socket\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Ok(true)` if either detection method finds a supervisor,\n    /// `Ok(false)` if no supervisor is detected.\n    /// Returns `Err` if detection fails.\n    pub fn detect_supervisor_direct(&self) -> Result<bool> {\n        // Check supervisor heartbeat file first\n        if self.check_supervisor_heartbeat_file()? {\n            return Ok(true);\n        }\n\n        // Fall back to socket check\n        if Self::check_supervisor_socket()? {\n            return Ok(true);\n        }\n\n        tracing::debug!(\"no supervisor detected via direct methods\");\n        Ok(false)\n    }\n\n    // ── Internal ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Write a heartbeat file atomically (write temp, then rename).\n    fn write_heartbeat(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let (state, current_bead, beads_processed, current_workspace, model, last_strand, adapter) = {\n            let guard = self\n                .shared_state\n                .lock()\n                .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"shared state lock poisoned: {e}\"))?;\n            (\n                guard.state.clone(),\n                guard.current_bead.clone(),\n                guard.beads_processed,\n                guard.current_workspace.clone(),\n                guard.model.clone(),\n                guard.last_strand.clone(),\n                guard.adapter.clone(),\n            )\n        };\n\n        // Use the current bead's workspace if set, otherwise fall back to home workspace.\n        let effective_workspace = current_workspace.unwrap_or_else(|| self.workspace.clone());\n\n        let is_idle = state == WorkerState::Exhausted || current_bead.is_none();\n        let current_task = current_bead.as_ref().map(|b| b.to_string());\n\n        // HOOP Hook 3 (heartbeat): append a JSONL line in HOOP's three-state\n        // format alongside the existing per-worker JSON file below. Best\n        // effort — see hoop_hooks module docs.\n        if state == WorkerState::Exhausted {\n            crate::hoop_hooks::emit_needle_heartbeat(\n                &effective_workspace,\n                &self.worker_id,\n                \"knot\",\n                serde_json::json!({\"reason\": \"strands exhausted\"}),\n            );\n        } else if let Some(ref bead_id) = current_bead {\n            crate::hoop_hooks::emit_needle_heartbeat(\n                &effective_workspace,\n                &self.worker_id,\n                \"executing\",\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead\": bead_id.to_string(),\n                    \"pid\": std::process::id(),\n                    \"adapter\": adapter,\n                }),\n            );\n        } else {\n            crate::hoop_hooks::emit_needle_heartbeat(\n                &effective_workspace,\n                &self.worker_id,\n                \"idle\",\n                serde_json::json!({\"last_strand\": last_strand}),\n            );\n        }\n\n        let data = HeartbeatData {\n            worker_id: self.worker_id.clone(),\n            qualified_id: self.qualified_id.clone(),\n            pid: std::process::id(),\n            state,\n            current_bead,\n            workspace: effective_workspace,\n            last_heartbeat: Utc::now(),\n            started_at: self.started_at,\n            beads_processed,\n            session: self.worker_id.clone(),\n            is_idle,\n            current_task,\n            model,\n            heartbeat_file: None,\n        };\n\n        let path = self.heartbeat_path();\n        let tmp_path = path.with_extension(\"json.tmp\");\n\n        // Auto-create parent directory so that heartbeats self-recover if the\n        // directory is deleted while a worker is running.\n        if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {\n            std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create heartbeat dir: {}\", parent.display()))?;\n        }\n\n        let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&data).context(\"failed to serialize heartbeat\")?;\n        std::fs::write(&tmp_path, json.as_bytes()).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to write temp heartbeat file: {}\",\n                tmp_path.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n        std::fs::rename(&tmp_path, &path).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to rename heartbeat file: {} -> {}\",\n                tmp_path.display(),\n                path.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Drop for HealthMonitor {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        // Best-effort: signal the emitter and clean up the heartbeat file.\n        self.stop();\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Utility functions\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Calculate the age of a heartbeat timestamp in seconds.\n///\n/// This function computes the time difference between the current time (`Utc::now()`)\n/// and the provided heartbeat timestamp, returning the age in seconds.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `timestamp` - The heartbeat timestamp to calculate age from\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `i64` - Age in seconds (0 for future timestamps, positive for past timestamps)\n///\n/// # Behavior\n///\n/// - Returns `0` for future timestamps (handles clock skew)\n/// - Returns accurate age in seconds for past timestamps\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use chrono::{Utc, TimeZone};\n/// use needle::health::calculate_heartbeat_age;\n///\n/// let past = Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::seconds(120);\n/// let age = calculate_heartbeat_age(past);\n/// assert_eq!(age, 120);\n///\n/// let future = Utc::now() + chrono::Duration::seconds(30);\n/// let age = calculate_heartbeat_age(future);\n/// assert_eq!(age, 0); // Clock skew handling\n/// ```\npub fn calculate_heartbeat_age(timestamp: DateTime<Utc>) -> i64 {\n    let now = Utc::now();\n    let duration = now.signed_duration_since(timestamp);\n\n    // Return 0 for future timestamps (handles clock skew)\n    // Return positive seconds for past timestamps\n    duration.num_seconds().max(0)\n}\n\n/// Clean up a heartbeat file by removing it from disk.\n///\n/// This function removes the heartbeat file at the given path. It handles\n/// both file-not-found (success) and unexpected error (failure) cases.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `path` - Path to the heartbeat file to remove\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(())` - If the file was removed successfully or doesn't exist\n/// * `Err(e)` - If removal fails for reasons other than NotFound\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use std::path::Path;\n/// use needle::health::cleanup_heartbeat_file;\n///\n/// let path = Path::new(\"/tmp/heartbeat.json\");\n/// cleanup_heartbeat_file(path)?;\n/// # Ok::<(), anyhow::Error>(())\n/// ```\npub fn cleanup_heartbeat_file(path: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n    match std::fs::remove_file(path) {\n        Ok(_) => Ok(()),\n        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {\n            // File doesn't exist - this is success (idempotent cleanup)\n            tracing::debug!(\n                path = %path.display(),\n                \"heartbeat file does not exist, skipping cleanup\"\n            );\n            Ok(())\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            // Log the error before returning - this ensures visibility of cleanup failures\n            tracing::warn!(\n                error = %e,\n                path = %path.display(),\n                \"failed to remove heartbeat file during cleanup\"\n            );\n            // Return with context for upstream handling\n            Err(e).with_context(|| format!(\"failed to remove heartbeat file: {}\", path.display()))\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a heartbeat file exists at the specified path.\n///\n/// This function provides simple presence detection for a heartbeat file,\n/// returning whether the file exists on disk without attempting to read\n/// or validate its contents.\n///\n/// This is useful for quick supervisor presence checks where you only need\n/// to know if a heartbeat file exists, not whether it's fresh or valid.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `path` - Path to the heartbeat file to check\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(true)` - If the heartbeat file exists\n/// * `Ok(false)` - If the heartbeat file does not exist\n/// * `Err(e)` - If a file system error occurs (e.g., permission denied)\n///\n/// # Errors\n///\n/// Returns an error if:\n/// - The path cannot be accessed due to permission issues\n/// - The path is a directory rather than a file\n/// - Other I/O errors occur\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use std::path::Path;\n/// use needle::health::check_heartbeat_file_exists;\n///\n/// let path = Path::new(\"/tmp/heartbeat.json\");\n/// match check_heartbeat_file_exists(path) {\n///     Ok(true) => println!(\"Heartbeat file exists\"),\n///     Ok(false) => println!(\"No heartbeat file found\"),\n///     Err(e) => eprintln!(\"Error checking for heartbeat: {}\", e),\n/// }\n/// # Ok::<(), anyhow::Error>(())\n/// ```\npub fn check_heartbeat_file_exists(path: &Path) -> Result<bool> {\n    // Inspect the directory entry first so a broken symlink remains\n    // distinguishable from a genuinely absent heartbeat file. `try_exists()`\n    // follows symlinks and reports both cases as `Ok(false)`.\n    match std::fs::symlink_metadata(path) {\n        Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {\n            tracing::debug!(path = %path.display(), \"heartbeat file does not exist\");\n            Ok(false)\n        }\n        Err(error) => Err(error).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to check heartbeat file existence: {}\",\n                path.display()\n            )\n        }),\n        Ok(_) => {\n            let metadata = std::fs::metadata(path).with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"failed to read metadata for heartbeat file: {}\",\n                    path.display()\n                )\n            })?;\n            if metadata.is_file() {\n                Ok(true)\n            } else {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    path = %path.display(),\n                    \"heartbeat path exists but is a directory, not a file\"\n                );\n                Ok(false)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// StalePeer\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A peer worker detected as having a stale heartbeat.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct StalePeer {\n    pub worker_id: String,\n    /// Fully-qualified identity of the peer.\n    pub qualified_id: Option<String>,\n    pub pid: u32,\n    pub pid_alive: bool,\n    pub current_bead: Option<BeadId>,\n    pub last_heartbeat: DateTime<Utc>,\n    pub heartbeat_file: PathBuf,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Emitter loop (runs in a dedicated std::thread)\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Maximum sleep between heartbeat attempts when backing off on failure.\nconst MAX_HEARTBEAT_BACKOFF: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5 * 60);\n\n/// Sleep interval for interruptible sleep — check shutdown flag every 100ms.\n///\n/// This ensures the heartbeat emitter responds to shutdown signals within 100ms\n/// instead of sleeping for the full heartbeat interval (default 60s). When the\n/// worker is killed (e.g., by the capacity governor), this gives the atexit\n/// handler a better chance to emit worker.stopped telemetry.\nconst INTERRUPTIBLE_SLEEP_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(100);\n\n/// Background emitter loop. Writes heartbeat at each interval.\n///\n/// Circuit breaker: after `max_consecutive_failures` consecutive write failures\n/// the loop sets the shutdown flag and exits so the worker terminates instead of\n/// spinning indefinitely.\n///\n/// Backoff: each consecutive failure doubles the inter-attempt sleep, capped at\n/// [`MAX_HEARTBEAT_BACKOFF`].\n///\n/// Uses an interruptible sleep pattern to respond quickly to shutdown signals.\n#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\nfn emitter_loop(\n    shared_state: Arc<Mutex<SharedHeartbeatState>>,\n    shutdown: Arc<AtomicBool>,\n    heartbeat_dir: PathBuf,\n    worker_id: String,\n    qualified_id: String,\n    workspace: PathBuf,\n    started_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n    interval: Duration,\n    max_consecutive_failures: u32,\n) {\n    // Ensure the heartbeat directory exists before entering the write loop so\n    // that workers self-recover if ~/.needle/state/heartbeats/ is deleted.\n    if let Err(e) = std::fs::create_dir_all(&heartbeat_dir) {\n        tracing::error!(\n            error = %e,\n            dir = %heartbeat_dir.display(),\n            \"failed to create heartbeat directory\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    let mut consecutive_failures: u32 = 0;\n    let mut current_sleep = interval;\n    let mut elapsed = Duration::ZERO;\n\n    loop {\n        // Interruptible sleep: check shutdown flag every 100ms instead of\n        // sleeping for the full interval. This ensures the emitter responds\n        // to shutdown signals quickly, giving the atexit handler a chance to\n        // emit worker.stopped telemetry even if the process is killed.\n        while elapsed < current_sleep {\n            if shutdown.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {\n                tracing::debug!(worker = %worker_id, \"heartbeat emitter shutting down\");\n                return;\n            }\n            let sleep_dur = std::cmp::min(INTERRUPTIBLE_SLEEP_INTERVAL, current_sleep - elapsed);\n            std::thread::sleep(sleep_dur);\n            elapsed += sleep_dur;\n        }\n        elapsed = Duration::ZERO;\n\n        let (state, current_bead, beads_processed, current_workspace, model) =\n            match shared_state.lock() {\n                Ok(guard) => (\n                    guard.state.clone(),\n                    guard.current_bead.clone(),\n                    guard.beads_processed,\n                    guard.current_workspace.clone(),\n                    guard.model.clone(),\n                ),\n                Err(_) => {\n                    // Mutex poisoned — the main thread panicked. Exit.\n                    tracing::error!(\n                        worker = %worker_id,\n                        \"shared state mutex poisoned, heartbeat emitter exiting\"\n                    );\n                    return;\n                }\n            };\n\n        // Use the current bead's workspace if set, otherwise fall back to home workspace.\n        let effective_workspace = current_workspace.unwrap_or_else(|| workspace.clone());\n\n        let is_idle = state == WorkerState::Exhausted || current_bead.is_none();\n        let current_task = current_bead.as_ref().map(|b| b.to_string());\n\n        let data = HeartbeatData {\n            worker_id: worker_id.clone(),\n            qualified_id: qualified_id.clone(),\n            pid: std::process::id(),\n            state,\n            current_bead,\n            workspace: effective_workspace,\n            last_heartbeat: Utc::now(),\n            started_at,\n            beads_processed,\n            session: worker_id.clone(),\n            is_idle,\n            current_task,\n            model,\n            heartbeat_file: None,\n        };\n\n        let path = heartbeat_dir.join(format!(\"{}.json\", qualified_id));\n        let tmp_path = path.with_extension(\"json.tmp\");\n\n        let write_result: anyhow::Result<()> = (|| {\n            // Re-assert the heartbeat directory on every attempt, not just once\n            // before the loop starts. If the directory (or an ancestor) is\n            // transiently removed or unavailable while the worker is running —\n            // e.g. an external cleanup process, a race with another tool, or a\n            // filesystem hiccup under load — the write below would otherwise\n            // fail with ENOENT on every subsequent attempt until the circuit\n            // breaker trips, since nothing else recreates it. `create_dir_all`\n            // is a cheap no-op when the directory already exists, so doing this\n            // unconditionally lets a single transient disruption self-heal\n            // within one heartbeat interval instead of killing the worker after\n            // `max_consecutive_failures` attempts (which, with the default\n            // backoff schedule, can take 25-30 minutes to trigger).\n            std::fs::create_dir_all(&heartbeat_dir)?;\n            let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&data)?;\n            std::fs::write(&tmp_path, json.as_bytes())?;\n            std::fs::rename(&tmp_path, &path)?;\n            Ok(())\n        })();\n\n        match write_result {\n            Ok(()) => {\n                consecutive_failures = 0;\n                current_sleep = interval;\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                consecutive_failures += 1;\n                tracing::error!(\n                    error = %e,\n                    worker = %worker_id,\n                    consecutive_failures,\n                    max = max_consecutive_failures,\n                    \"heartbeat write failed\"\n                );\n                if consecutive_failures >= max_consecutive_failures {\n                    tracing::error!(\n                        worker = %worker_id,\n                        consecutive_failures,\n                        \"heartbeat emitter circuit breaker triggered — worker will shut down\"\n                    );\n                    // Emit a final heartbeat event before shutting down so the\n                    // telemetry log shows the circuit breaker was the cause.\n                    let _ = std::fs::write(\n                        heartbeat_dir.join(format!(\"{}-circuit-breaker.txt\", qualified_id)),\n                        format!(\n                            \"Circuit breaker tripped after {} consecutive heartbeat write failures\\n\\\n                             Worker: {}\\n\\\n                             Qualified ID: {}\\n\\\n                             Last error: {}\\n\\\n                             Timestamp: {}\",\n                            consecutive_failures,\n                            worker_id,\n                            qualified_id,\n                            e,\n                            Utc::now().to_rfc3339()\n                        ),\n                    );\n                    shutdown.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);\n                    return;\n                }\n                // Exponential backoff to reduce log spam before the circuit breaker fires.\n                current_sleep = current_sleep.saturating_mul(2).min(MAX_HEARTBEAT_BACKOFF);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use std::time::Duration;\n\n    /// Serialises the tests that mutate `NEEDLE_SUPERVISOR_SOCKET`.\n    ///\n    /// `std::env::set_var`/`remove_var` mutate process-global state while the\n    /// test harness runs tests on parallel threads, so one test's `remove_var`\n    /// could land between another's `set_var` and its assertion.   .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner())\n    }\n\n    /// Isolates the test's HOME directory to a temp directory, preventing tests\n    /// from writing to the live fleet's state directory  /// may call `dirs_or_home()` which reads HOME directly.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```ignore\n    /// let _home_guard = isolate_test_home();\n    /// let dir = HomeGuard {\n            _temp_dir: temp_dir,\n            original_home,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Guard that restores HOME to its original value when dropped.\n    struct HomeGuard {\n          Some(home) => std::env::set_var(\"HOME\", home),\n                None => std::env::remove_var(\"HOME\"),\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn test_config(heartbeat_dir: &Path) -> failures:\n    /// the emitter must set the shutdown flag and return rather than looping forever.\n    #[test]\n    fn emitter_exits_after_consecutive_failures() {\n        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;\n\n        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();\n        let hb_dir = dir.path().join(\"state\").join(\"heartbeats\");\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&hb_dir).unwrap();\n\n        // Make the heartbeat directory read-only so every write attempt fails.\n        std::fs::set_permissions(&hb_dir, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o555)).unwrap();\n\n        // Verify the directory is actually unwritable. When running as root\n        // (e.g., in CI containers), 0o555 doesn't block writes and the emitter\n        // loop would never hit its failure threshold, hanging the test forever.\n        let probe = hb_dir.join(\".write-probe\");\n        let unwritable = std::fs::write(&probe, b\"x\").is_err();\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&probe);\n        if !unwritable {\n            // Root bypasses permission checks — skip this test.\n            let _ = std::fs::set_permissions(&hb_dir, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755));\n            return;\n        }\n\n        let shared_state = Arc::new(Mutex::new(SharedHeartbeatState {\n            state: WorkerState::Selecting,\n            current_bead: None,\n            beads_processed: 0,\n            current_workspace: None,\n            model: \"claude-sonnet-4\".to_string(),\n            last_strand: None,\n            adapter: None,\n        }));\n        let shutdown = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));\n\n        let shutdown_clone = shutdown.clone();\n        let shared_state_clone = shared_state.clone();\n        let hb_dir_clone = hb_dir.clone();\n\n        // Use a tiny interval and a low failure threshold so the test completes quickly.\n        let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {\n            emitter_loop(\n                shared_state_clone,\n                shutdown_clone,\n                hb_dir_clone,\n                \"cb-test\".to_string(),\n                \"claude-cb-test\".to_string(),\n                PathBuf::from(\"/tmp\"),\n                Utc::now(),\n                Duration::from_millis(1),\n                3, // trip after 3 consecutive failures\n            );\n        });\n\n        handle.join().expect(\"emitter thread panicked\");\n\n        // The circuit breaker must have set the shutdown flag.\n        assert!(\n            shutdown.load(Ordering::SeqCst),\n            \"shutdown flag must be set after circuit breaker trips\"\n        );\n\n        // Restore permissions so the tempdir can be cleaned up.\n        let _ = std::fs::set_permissions(&hb_dir, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755));\n    }\n\n    #[tokio::test]\n    async fn heartbeat file creation and periodic refresh.\n    ///\n    /// This test validates the acceptance criteria:\n    /// 1. Workers create heartbeat file on startup\n    /// 2. Heartbeat file is refreshed every heartbeat_interval_secs\n    /// 3. File contains worker ID and last refresh timestamp\n    ///\n    /// Uses tokio virtual time to test 30-second refresh intervals without\n    /// waiting for real wall-clock time.\n    #[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]\n    async fn heartbeat_creates_and_refreshes_every_30_seconds() {\n        let _home_guard = isolate_test_home();\n        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();\n        let _hb_dir = dir.path().join(\"state\").join(\"heartbeats\");\n\n        let mut config = Config::default();\n        config.workspace.home = dir.path().to_path_buf();\n        // Use a one-second interval so the test exercises the real emitter\n        // without spending a minute and a half waiting on wall-clock time.\n        config.health.heartbeat_interval_secs = 1;\n        config.health.heartbeat_ttl_secs = 300;\n\n        let mut monitor = HealthMonitor::new(\n            config,\n            \"validate-worker\".to_string(),\n            Telemetry::new(\"test\".to_string()),\n            None,\n        );\n\n        let path = monitor.heartbeat_path();\n\n        // ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 1: Worker creates heartbeat file on startup\n        monitor.start_emitter().unwrap();\n        assert!(\n            path.exists(),\n            \"heartbeat file must be created immediately on startup\"\n        );\n\n        // Verify initial heartbeat contains required fields\n        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap();\n        let data: HeartbeatData = serde_json::from_str(&content).unwrap();\n\n        // ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 3a: File contains worker ID\n        assert_eq!(data.worker_id, \"validate-worker\");\n        assert!(!data.qualified_id.is_empty());\n        assert_eq!(data.qualified_id, format!(\"{}-validate-worker\", data.model));\n\n        // ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 3b: File contains last refresh timestamp\n        let initial_timestamp = data.last_heartbeat;\n        let now = Utc::now();\n        let age = (now - initial_timestamp).num_seconds().abs();\n        assert!(\n            age < 2,\n            \"initial heartbeat timestamp must be within 2 seconds of now, got {} seconds difference\",\n            age\n        );\n\n        // Verify PID is included (useful for detecting crashed workers)\n        assert_eq!(data.pid, std::process::id());\n\n        // Verify started_at timestamp\n        assert!(!data.started_at.timestamp().is_negative());\n\n        // ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 2: File updates every ~30 seconds\n        // We'll observe 3 refresh cycles to ensure periodic updates\n        for cycle in 1..=3 {\n            tracing::info!(\"waiting for heartbeat refresh cycle {} of 3\", cycle);\n\n            // Record the timestamp before waiting\n            let before_content = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap();\n            let before_data: HeartbeatData = serde_json::from_str(&before_content).unwrap();\n            let before_timestamp = before_data.last_heartbeat;\n\n            // Wait for at least one one-second refresh.\n            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(2));\n\n            // Verify the file has been updated\n            let after_content = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap();\n            let after_data: HeartbeatData = serde_json::from_str(&after_content).unwrap();\n            let after_timestamp = after_data.last_heartbeat;\n\n            let time_diff = (after_timestamp - before_timestamp).num_seconds();\n\n            // The timestamp should have advanced by approximately the interval\n            // Allow some tolerance for system load and scheduling delays\n            assert!(\n                (1..=3).contains(&time_diff),\n                \"heartbeat should refresh every ~1 second, got {} seconds difference between updates (cycle {})\",\n                time_diff,\n                cycle\n            );\n\n            // Verify the timestamp continues to advance monotonically\n            assert!(\n                after_timestamp > before_timestamp,\n                \"last_heartbeat timestamp must monotonically increase\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Final verification: heartbeat file still contains valid data\n        let final_content = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap();\n        let final_data: HeartbeatData = serde_json::from_str(&final_content).unwrap();\n\n        assert_eq!(final_data.worker_id, \"validate-worker\");\n        assert!(!final_data.qualified_id.is_empty());\n        assert_eq!(final_data.pid, std::process::id());\n\n        monitor.stop();\n\n        // Verify file is removed after stop\n        assert!(\n            !path.exists(),\n            \"heartbeat file must be removed when worker stops\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// Test that validates heartbeat cleanup on graceful shutdown (SIGTERM).\n    ///\n    /// This test verifies the acceptance criteria:\n    /// - Workers remove heartbeat file on graceful shutdown\n    /// - Stopped worker's heartbeat file is deleted\n    /// -    let _home_guard = isolate_test_home();\n        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();\n        let _hb_dir = dir.path().join(\"state\").join(\"heartbeats\");\n\n        let mut config = Phase: RateLimiter setup\n        let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::InitStepStarted {\n            step: \"rate_limiter_setup\".to_string(),\n        });\n        let rate_limiter_start = Instant::now();\n        let registry = Registry::default_location(&config.workspace.home);\n        let rate_limiter =\n            RateLimiter::new(config.limits.clone(), &config.workspace.home.join(\"state\"));\n        let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::InitStepCompleted {\n            step: \"rate_limiter_setup\".to_string(),\n            duration_ms: rate_limiter_start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64,\n        });\n\n        // Phase: MitosisEvaluator setup\n        let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::InitStepStarted {\n            step: \"mitosis_evaluator_setup\".to_string(),\n        });\n        let mitosis_start = Instant::now();\n        let mitosis_evaluator = MitosisEvaluator::new(\n            config.strands.mitosis.clone(),\n            telemetry.clone(),\n            std::path::PathBuf::from(\"/tmp\"),\n        );\n        let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::InitStepCompleted {\n            step: \"mitosis_evaluator_setup\".to_string(),\n            duration_ms: mitosis_start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64,\n        });\n\n        // Phase: Registry state restoration\n        let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::InitStepStarted {\n            step: \"registry_state_restoration\".to_string(),\n        });\n        let registry_start = Instant::now();\n        // Restore beads_processed from registry if this worker was previously registered\n        // (e.g., hot-reload resume). New workers start at 0.\n        // Match by qualified identity ({adapter}-{worker_id}).\n        let qualified_id = format!(\"{}-{}\", config.agent.default, worker_name);\n        let beads_processed = registry\n            .list()\n            .ok()\n            .and_then(|workers| workers.into_iter().find(|w| w.id == qualified_id))\n            .map(|entry| entry.beads_processed)\n            .unwrap_or(0);\n        let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::InitStepCompleted {\n            step: \"registry_state_restoration\".to_string(),\n            duration_ms: registry_start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64,\n        });\n\n        let default_workspace = config.workspace.default.clone();\n\n        // Create the watchdog trigger flag before creating the Worker.\n        let watchdog_triggered = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));\n\n        let worker = Worker {\n            config,\n            worker_name,\n            home_store: store.clone(),\n            store,\n            telemetry,\n            strands,\n            claimer,\n            prompt_builder,\n            dispatcher,\n            outcome_handler,\n            health,\n            registry,\n            rate_limiter,\n            mitosis_evaluator,\n            state: WorkerState::Booting,\n            current_bead: None,\n            exclusion_set: HashSet::new(),\n            race_lost_exclusions: Vec::new(),\n            race_lost_this_cycle: HashSet::new(),\n            retry_count: 0,\n            consecutive_race_lost: 0,\n            beads_processed,\n            shutdown,\n            last_error: None,\n            boot_time: None,\n            built_prompt: None,\n            current_strand: None,\n            exec_output: None,\n            exec_started_at: None,\n            last_effort: None,\n            pre_dispatch_head: None,\n            current_workspace: default_workspace,\n            booting_emitted,\n            last_waterfall_restarts: 0,\n            last_restart_triggers: Vec::new(),\n            last_strand_evaluations: Vec::new(),\n            handling_state_entered_at: None,\n            watchdog_triggered: watchdog_triggered.clone(),\n            watchdog_handle: None,\n            bead_lifecycle_span: None,\n            last_outcome: None,\n            last_workspace_mtime: None,\n            found_but_excluded: false,\n            spawn_path_metadata: None,\n        };\n\n        // Warn if both budget thresholds are disabled (0.0 = no cap).\n        if worker.config.budget.warn_usd <= 0.0 && worker.config.budget.stop_usd <= 0.0 {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                warn_usd = 0.0,\n                stop_usd = 0.0,\n                \"Budget enforcement is DISABLED: both warn_usd and stop_usd are set to 0.0. \\\n                 Daily spend is fully uncapped — no warnings, no halting. \\\n                 To enable budget protection, set non-zero values in .needle.yaml under 'budget:' \\\n                 (e.g., 'budget: {{warn_usd: 10.0, stop_usd: 50.0}}'). \\\n                 For fleet-wide governance, consider claude-governor (https://github.com/jedarden/claude-governor).\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        worker\n    }\n\n    /// Start the watchdog thread that monitors HANDLING state duration.\n    ///\n    /// The watchdog runs in a separate thread (not part of the Tokio runtime)\n    /// and can detect when the worker is stuck in HANDLING state even if\n    /// the Tokio runtime becomes wedged. If HANDLING state exceeds the\n    /// timeout, the watchdog sets the `watchdog_triggered` flag, which\n    /// the main worker loop checks to force recovery.\n    fn start_watchdog_thread(&mut self) {\n        let watchdog_triggered = self.watchdog_triggered.clone();\n        let handling_state_entered_at_ptr =\n            &self.handling_state_entered_at as *const Option<Instant> as usize;\n\n        let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {\n            loop {\n                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(5));\n                if watchdog_triggered.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {\n                    // Watchdog has already triggered, exit the thread.\n                    break;\n                }\n                // Check if we've been in HANDLING state for too long.\n                // We read the timestamp from the Worker struct via the pointer.\n                // SAFETY: The Worker struct outlives the watchdog thread because\n                // the thread is joined when the Worker is dropped.\n                let entered_at = unsafe {\n                    let ptr = handling_state_entered_at_ptr as *const Option<Instant>;\n                    (*ptr).as_ref().copied()\n                };\n\n                if let Some(entry_time) = entered_at {\n                    let elapsed = entry_time.elapsed().as_secs();\n                    if elapsed >= HANDLING_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_SECS {\n                        tracing::error!(\n                            elapsed_secs = elapsed,\n                            \"HANDLING state watchdog triggered - forcing recovery\"\n                        );\n                        watchdog_triggered.store(true, Ordering::Release);\n                        break;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        });\n\n        self.watchdog_handle = Some(handle);\n    }\n\n    /// Run the worker loop until exhausted, stopped, or errored.\n    ///\n    /// The main loop is a match on `self.state`. Every state has a handler\n    /// that performs its actions and sets `self.state` to the next state.\n    ///\n    /// Guarantees that the telemetry BufWriter is flushed before returning,\n    /// even when the inner state machine exits early via `?`.\n    pub async fn run(&mut self) -> Result<WorkerState> {\n        // Start the telemetry writer now that we are inside the tokio runtime.\n        self.telemetry.start();\n\n        // IMMEDIATE boot event — must be the first thing emitted after telemetry starts.\n        // This ensures we get a trace even if subsequent init steps block indefinitely.\n        // Skip if already emitted externally (e.g., from CLI layer for early boot diagnostics).\n        if !self.booting_emitted {\n            self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::WorkerBooting {\n                worker_name: self.worker_name.clone(),\n                version: env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\").to_string(),\n            })?;\n            // Force-flush to disk before boot() — if init blocks, we still have a trace.\n            self.telemetry\n                .force_flush_async(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))\n                .await?;\n        }\n\n        let result = self.run_inner().await;\n\n        // Safety-net flush: shutdown() is idempotent.
